snippet.title: Sleep Historian
snippet.description:
Welcome to Sleep Historian – where forgotten history gently lulls you to sleep.

Each night, we uncover the world’s hidden past: ancient civilizations, forbidden knowledge, lost technologies, secret societies, and timelines that challenge everything you thought you knew.

Through calm narration, cinematic storytelling, and deep historical research, we explore topics like:
• Vatican conspiracies & Freemason secrets
• The Phantom Time Hypothesis & erased centuries
• Lost cities, forbidden books, and ancient cover-ups
• Templars, Assassins, and empires that vanished

Whether you're seeking relaxation, sleep, or late-night curiosity – this channel is your sanctuary for truth beneath the silence.

📜 New episodes every week.
🎧 Best with headphones & dim lights.

Subscribe and let time drift away…

#SleepHistorian #RelaxingHistory #AncientSecrets #BedtimeMysteries #HistoryToSleepTo  #HistoryForSleep

snippet.title: History Time
snippet.description:
Travel back in time with me to some of the most fascinating moments in human history. Witness colossal sea battles involving tens of thousands of men, take part in pagan blood rituals in the mysterious forests of Northern Europe and engage in highly orchestrated tribal warfare within Pre-Columbian Mesoamerica. All this and more from the comfort of your own living room/bus to work/toilet throne.

Established in early 2017, History Time is researched, written, filmed, narrated & produced by Pete Kelly - public educator from the UK with history degrees at undergraduate and postgraduate level.

Guest writers include historians, authors and archaeologists such as Dr Raoul McLaughlin, Dr David Frye, Dr David Miano & Gordon Doherty.

Original music is composed for the channel by Joss Edwards, Brodie Marshall & Matt Hunt

No AI is used. 

Sign up to my free mailing list for adventures at the worlds greatest archaeological sites-
http://historytimewithpete.substack.com

snippet.title: Mr. Deep History
snippet.description:
Mr. Deep History is a calm platform for science-based storytelling from origins to empires. Longform essays on human evolution, archaeology, early civilizations, and how societies change, survive, and collapse - no hype, just the record, told slowly. Designed to help you slow down, focus, and drift off if you want to: perfect for deep work, long walks, late-night thinking, and sleep.

 Episodes are built with respect for evidence, drawing on archaeology, primary texts when available, and modern research. We use AI tools to assist parts of the workflow (research support, drafting, narration, imagery), then edit and polish for clarity and accuracy.

 These videos blend research with documentary-style storytelling for learning and atmosphere - not a substitute for academic or professional advice. Reconstructions are interpretive, and all visuals are AI-generated artistic impressions.

Sit back. Listen. Relax. Think. Thanks for being here 😊

snippet.title: Ancestors Civilization
snippet.description:
Long-Form History Documentaries exploring the civilizations that shaped the modern world as we know it today.

Thanks for being Here

Content Creation Process

Step 1: We have a team of 10 members, including 4 scriptwriters and 1 senior scriptwriter. The scriptwriters independently research the assigned topic using multiple reliable sources and collect relevant information.

Step 2: The collected information is compiled into a script and reviewed, edited, and approved by the senior scriptwriter to ensure accuracy, originality, and quality.

Step 3: After approval, the finalized script is sent to a professional voiceover artist for narration.

Step 4: Once the voiceover is received, our creative team creates original visuals based on the script and narration.

Step 5: All visuals, voiceover, and information are carefully synchronized, reviewed, and finalized before uploading the video.

snippet.title: ReligionForBreakfast
snippet.description:
An educational channel dedicated to the academic, nonsectarian study of religion. We promote improving the public's religious literacy by exploring humanity's beliefs and rituals through an anthropological, sociological, and archaeological lens. 

Religion for Breakfast does not endorse any particular religious tradition or non-religious perspective. Please be respectful in the comments!

The host, Dr. Andrew M. Henry, is a scholar of religious studies. His research focus is early Christianity and late Roman religion. He earned his PhD at Boston University. Follow him on Twitter @andrewmarkhenry.

These videos are freely available here on YouTube. If you are an instructor, feel free to use the YouTube link to my videos in your syllabi and classrooms. I do not permit downloading my videos and re-uploading them to a separate site or channel. This is called freebooting, and it violates Religion for Breakfast's copyright.

snippet.title: National Capital Area Skeptics (NCAS)
snippet.description:
The National Capital Area Skeptics (NCAS) is an independent 501(c)3 nonprofit organization dedicated to science, critical thinking, and scientific literacy. Founded in 1987 in the Washington, D.C. area, we bring you lectures and conversations with leading scientists, historians, archaeologists, and researchers on topics ranging from ancient history and archaeology to media literacy, misinformation, conspiracy theories, and the paranormal.

Our videos feature experts in science, history, and skeptical inquiry — including talks on ancient civilizations, UFOs and UAP, pseudoscience, climate science, public health, and the history of science. We believe that understanding how to evaluate evidence is as important as knowing what the evidence says.

Subscribe to stay current with our lecture series. Support our work at ncas.org.

snippet.title: The Long Now Foundation
snippet.description:
Launched by Stewart Brand in 02003, Long Now Talks has invited more than 400 leading thinkers to share their civilization-scale ideas with a live audience and millions around the globe tuning in to our podcast and videos. Long Now Talks are brought to you by The Long Now Foundation, which has spent the last 25 years igniting cultural imagination around long-term thinking.

By inspiring thought and conversation about how we've been shaped by the last 10,000 years and what might be in store for us over the next 10,000 years, Long Now Talks seek to expand our collective sense of the present moment. Long Now Talks cover futurism and speculative fiction; time, nature, and contemplative practices; the intersection of the humanities and sciences; the evolution of counterculture to cyberculture; cultural imagination, land art and public monuments; and, of course, long-term thinking and being a good ancestor.

Follow me on Twitter! https://twitter.com/AltHistoryHub

snippet.title: Lost Empires Archive
snippet.description:
Journey with us through the ruins of history's greatest empires - from the mysterious Mesopotamian kingdoms to the fallen glory of Rome, from the warrior cultures of the Celts and Goths to the nomadic conquests of the Huns. Each week, we uncover the untold stories of civilizations that once ruled the world but now exist only in archaeological fragments and ancient texts.

Our documentaries combine cutting-edge historical research with immersive storytelling, bringing you face-to-face with the emperors, warriors, and ordinary people who shaped the ancient world. Discover how these mighty empires rose to power, flourished for centuries, and ultimately met their end - leaving behind only whispers in stone and legend.

From the Epic of Gilgamesh to the last days of Byzantium, from Celtic druids to Gothic kingdoms, Lost Empires Archive is your gateway to understanding the civilizations that laid the foundation for our modern world.

snippet.description:
Welcome! 

We’re an educational YouTube channel made up of entertainment enthusiasts with backgrounds in game design, television production, literature and academia. Our team creates animated video essays about world history, mythology, and other subjects, all of which may or may not involve a cat!

EXTRA HISTORY
History is the best novel you've ever read. Join us Saturdays as we explore dramatic adventures in world history! 

EXTRA MYTHOLOGY
Our myths define us. They are the basis of our culture. Join us every other Wednesday as we delve into some of the coolest stories of world mythology!

SO YOU HAVEN'T READ

snippet.title: Fading Lore
snippet.description:
Hi there, my name is Paul and I started Fading Lore because I believe the most fascinating stories are the ones that are fading from our collective memory. My commitment to you is that every story on this channel is built on a foundation of deep research and rigorous fact-checking.

To deliver these stories, I aim for the clearest and most consistent listening experience possible. Let's just say I wasn't born with a 'voice for radio,' haha, so I utilize a high-quality synthetic narrator to ensure the story itself is always the star of the show.

In that same spirit of transparency, many of the visuals you see are also created with the help of modern AI tools. My role as the creator is to be the editor-in-chief: guiding the entire process, personally verifying every detail, and making sure the final documentary is a story you can trust and enjoy.

If you're a curious mind who loves history and folklore without the hype, I'm glad you're here.
